jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Plant Interaction Ecology (m/f/d) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction EcologySenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01.02.2027 :Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Plant Interaction Ecology(Full-Time / Part-Time ** ** options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.The announced position is part of a newly established research group studying plant environment interactions. The successful candidate will contribute to shaping the group's research programme and develop an independent research project aligned with the group's broader interests.Your tasks- Conduct internationally recognized research on how plant-animal interactions shape plant regeneration- Advance a mechanistic understanding of how plant-animal interactions and regeneration processes influence plant responses to climate and land-use change, e.g., shifts in species ranges or ecological novelty- Design and conduct field experiments, e.g., testing drivers of plant establishment, intraspecific variability, or the role of animal-mediated seed dispersal in forest dynamics- Develop and apply ecological models that integrate experimental findings with long-term datasets, linking individual-level processes to population dynamics and species range shifts- Publish research findings in leading international, peer-reviewed journals- Develop competitive proposals for third-party research funding- Supervise and mentor BSc, MSc, and PhD students- Contribute to teaching at the Bachelor’s and Master’s levels- Contribute to the development of the Interaction Ecology and Climate research groupYour profile- A doctoral degree, completed or nearing completion, in ecology, botany, biology, or a closely related field- A strong background in ecology, with research experience in plant ecology and or interactions between plants and animals- Demonstrated experience in designing and conducting field experiments- Experience conducting fieldwork under challenging conditions, e.g., in alpine environments or remote forest areas- Strong quantitative skills, including experience with advanced statistical methods such as Bayesian hierarchical models and data integration (combining heterogeneous datasets) and/or demographic or process-based population models, preferably using R- A strong publication record relative to career stage- Motivation to develop independent research on plant regeneration and biotic interactions in the context of climate and land-use change- Ability to work independently and collaboratively, and a willingness to contribute to teaching and student supervision- Fluency in spoken and written EnglishDesirable skills- An interest in science communication and public outreach- Proficiency in German, particularly for contributing to teaching and outreach activitiesWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with a full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees) as a single PDF by 13 December 2026.Apply online via:https://short.sg/j/68770090by pressing the "Apply now" ButtonApplications via email cannot be considered.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Eike Lena Neuschulz at:eike-lena.neuschulz@senckenberg.de****For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.
